newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: YTL says withdrawing from CEPA bid.
newsitem.headline: YTL says withdrawing from CEPA bid.

text.p: Malaysia's YTL Corp Bhd said on Tuesday that it has decided to withdraw a $2.6 billion offer to buy the entire stake in Hong Kong power firm Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA).
YTL managing director Francis Yeoh told a news conference that CEPA's parent Hopewell Holdings Ltd could not assure him that Hopewell shareholders would commit themselves to the offer.
"In these circumstances, YTL announces that it has irrevocably decided not to make any offer," Yeoh said.
Hopewell has earlier agreed to sell most of its 60 percent stake in CEPA to U.S. utility firm Southern Co's Southern Electric International.
YTL also announced on Tuesday that it would group all of its power generation interest under a new company to called YTL Power International and float it on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
Yeoh told the conference that YTL Power International would be listed under the new guidelines for listing of infrastructure project companies.

YTL Corp, one of the five independent power producers in the country, has a plant each in Terengganu and Johor states with a total capacity of 1,212 megawatts. Both plants have been generating electricity since October 1994.
